title: The Travelling Book
synopsis: The library lent its oldest book, the Book of Maps, to the city museum.
A courier took it on the night train.
The book never came to the museum.
goal: Follow the courier's trail and find out who has the Book of Maps.

options.label: The dinosaur museum
options.feedback: The letter talks about mummies and a stone. Are they in this poster?

options.label: The train and bus museum
options.feedback: The courier does not write about trains or buses.

options.label: The space museum
options.feedback: Rockets and planets are not in the letter. Read it again.

notes: Played as a look round (ExploreScene): the courier's suitcase on the bench holds his letter; the poster board opens once it is read.
Sandbox only: the station picture, its measured areas and the posters are London Case 01's.

learning.objective: 편지의 'old mummies and a famous stone'을 읽고 같은 것이 그려진 박물관 포스터를 고른다.

play.title: The Courier's Suitcase
story: The courier is not here, but his suitcase is.
It sits alone on a bench.
play.letter:
Dear Ms. Rosa,
I have the Book of Maps with me.
I will take it to the museum with the old mummies and the famous stone.
They will keep it safe.
— The courier
play.question: Which museum is the courier going to?
hints: Find the suitcase on the bench and read the letter first.
Look at each poster. Which one shows mummies and a big stone?
transition: The poster shows a golden mummy case and a stone covered in writing.
Did the book get to the museum?

play.title: The Guard's Report
story: At the museum, a guard is waiting.
"A man came in last night with a suitcase," he says.
"He did not leave a book. But he left three things."
play.letter:
Three strange things in the gallery:
The button is red. It is under the bench.
The cloth is blue. It is on the frame.
The footprint is wet. It is next to the door.
— The night guard
play.question: Which thing shows the way the man went out?
hints: Read each line of the report. Each one says where a thing is.
Look for the words 'next to the door'. The man went out that way.
transition: The wet footprint points out of the door.
Outside the museum is the market hall.
Someone there may have seen the man.

play.title: Three Witnesses
story: The market hall is busy, even late at night.
Three people work near the museum door.
Did they see the man with the suitcase?
play.letter:
Ask the witnesses what they saw.
Find two people who saw him carry the same thing.
play.question: What did the man carry?
hints: Ask every witness the same question: What did he carry?
Two witnesses say the same thing. Compare their answers.
play.successMessage: Two witnesses saw the same thing!
transition: The man carried a black case with straps.
And the juggler remembers his grey hat.
"He went to the lost property room at the station," says the baker.

play.title: The Lost Property Room
story: Back at the station, a small room is full of lost things.
"A man left a case here last night," the clerk says.
play.letter:
LOST PROPERTY — LAST NIGHT
A man in a dark coat left a case here.
The case is black. It has two brown straps and a paper label.
He said, "A friend will come for it."
play.question: Which one did the man leave?
hints: Read the note again: what colour is the case?
Look at each picture for two brown straps and a paper label.
transition: Inside the case is the Book of Maps, safe and dry!
A paper label hangs on the handle.
There is writing on the label.

clue.note: The black case with two brown straps holds the Book of Maps.

play.title: The Label
story: Ms. Rosa holds the Book of Maps.
"Thank you, detective! But who was it for?"
You read the paper label again.
play.letterIntro: The label on the case says:
play.letter:
Please keep this case for my friend in the grey hat.
He will take the book to the museum in the morning.
— The courier
play.question: Who is the courier's friend?
hints: The label says the friend has a grey hat.
Open your witness notes. Which witness talked about a grey hat?
transition: The juggler laughs. "Yes, the courier is my friend!"
"He missed his train, so he left the book with me."
Tomorrow the Book of Maps goes to the museum, with a detective to watch it.

objectives: Find where the courier was going.
Search the museum and talk to the witnesses.

intro: The library lent its oldest book to the city museum.
A courier took the Book of Maps on the night train.
This morning the museum called: the book never came!
play.caseSummary: The courier went to the museum, out of the gallery and past the market hall. Two witnesses saw his black case. You found it at lost property, with the Book of Maps inside, kept for his friend in the grey hat.

notes: STEP 3-13: planned by Claude Code to try the puzzles played on pictures in the sandbox: a look round (M1), a search (M2), a talk with witnesses (M3), a picture choice with hidden names (M4), and a text final whose answer is a statement of M3.
Sandbox only: every picture is a London bundled picture with its measured areas. A real season plans its own (assets.manifest.json).
